external_entities.name: colleague
external_entities.description: A colleague who signs in through the identity broker and uses applications.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Colleagues sign in to it from wherever they are, including their own devices at home.

external_entities.name: franchise colleague
external_entities.description: A franchise colleague whose own identity provider vouches for them.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Franchise colleagues do not have staff accounts with us; their own identity provider vouches for them

external_entities.name: HR system
external_entities.description: The HR system that supplies group membership changes and leaver information overnight.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Group membership is not maintained there by hand — it comes from the HR system overnight.

external_entities.name: identity provider
external_entities.description: The identity provider used by franchise colleagues to vouch for them.
external_entities.source_excerpt: their own identity provider vouches for them
external_entities.notes: The text does not identify which colleagues this provider is allowed to vouch for.

processes.name: identity broker
processes.description: Signs colleagues in, issues tokens, signs tokens, accepts franchise identity-provider sign-ins, pulls HR changes, and writes audit events.
processes.source_excerpt: Everything colleagues use signs them in through one identity broker.

processes.name: store admin console
processes.description: An application that uses the token's groups to authorize price changes and transaction voids across stores.
processes.source_excerpt: The store admin console is one of those applications.
processes.notes: The console does not check which store the colleague belongs to, so a store-manager token works against every store.

data_stores.name: key store
data_stores.description: A store containing the signing key used by the identity broker.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The broker signs tokens with a signing key it keeps in a key store.

data_stores.name: directory
data_stores.description: The identity broker's directory containing colleagues and their group memberships.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The broker keeps the colleagues and the groups they are in its own directory.

data_stores.name: audit log
data_stores.description: A log to which the broker writes sign-ins.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The broker writes sign-ins to an audit log.
data_stores.notes: Nobody has written down what the log records or whether it covers the franchise route.

data_flows.name: sign-in
data_flows.description: A colleague signs in through the identity broker.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Colleagues sign in to it from wherever they are, including their own devices at home.

data_flows.name: issue token
data_flows.description: The identity broker issues a token to a signed-in colleague.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Once the broker has signed a colleague in it issues them a token.
data_flows.notes: The token carries the colleague's staff id and a list of the groups they are in.
data_flows.data_description: token containing staff id and group list

data_flows.name: use console
data_flows.description: A colleague presents a token and uses the store admin console to change prices or void transactions.
data_flows.source_excerpt: If the token has the store-manager group in it, the console lets the holder change prices and void transactions.
data_flows.data_description: token, price changes, and transaction voids

data_flows.name: fetch public key
data_flows.description: The store admin console fetches the public half of the signing key from the identity broker.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Applications fetch the public half from the broker to check the signature.
data_flows.data_description: public half of the token-signing key

data_flows.name: read signing key
data_flows.description: The identity broker uses the signing key kept in the key store to sign tokens.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker signs tokens with a signing key it keeps in a key store.

data_flows.name: pull changes
data_flows.description: The HR system supplies overnight group-membership and leaver changes to the identity broker.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker pulls the changes once a night
data_flows.notes: The description says the broker pulls the changes, but the HR system is the source of those changes.

data_flows.name: maintain directory
data_flows.description: The identity broker reads and updates colleague and group records in its directory.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker keeps the colleagues and the groups they are in its own directory.

data_flows.name: write sign-ins
data_flows.description: The identity broker writes sign-in events to the audit log.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker writes sign-ins to an audit log.
data_flows.notes: It is unknown whether the franchise route is covered and what the log records.

data_flows.name: franchise sign-in
data_flows.description: A franchise colleague signs in through the broker using a vouch from the franchise identity provider.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Franchise colleagues do not have staff accounts with us; their own identity provider vouches for them and the broker takes that as a sign-in.

data_flows.name: vouch for colleague
data_flows.description: The franchise identity provider vouches for a franchise colleague to the identity broker.
data_flows.source_excerpt: their own identity provider vouches for them and the broker takes that as a sign-in.
data_flows.notes: The text does not state which colleagues the provider is allowed to vouch for.

trust_boundaries.name: corporate network
trust_boundaries.description: The corporate network on which the identity broker and store admin console run.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The broker runs on the corporate network.

trust_boundaries.name: home
trust_boundaries.description: The home environment containing colleagues' own devices used to sign in.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: including their own devices at home

trust_boundaries.name: franchise stores
trust_boundaries.description: The franchise environment whose colleagues are admitted through their own identity provider.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: We also let the franchise stores in.

assumptions.assumption: The directory is confidential because it contains colleagues and their group memberships.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the directory keeps colleagues and the groups they are in.

assumptions.assumption: The key store is confidential because it contains a signing key.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the key store contains the signing key used to sign tokens.
